value.body: Indian Railways fills most of its non-officer posts through Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), using centralised notifications (CENs) and computer-based tests. Major exams include NTPC (station master, goods train manager, clerks, ticket staff), Junior Engineer (JE), Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) and Technicians, Paramedical staff, Ministerial & Isolated categories, and Level-1 (Group D) posts.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Eligibility depends on the post: Class 10 / ITI for Level-1 and ALP / Technician posts, Class 12 for undergraduate-level NTPC posts, any degree for graduate-level NTPC posts, a diploma or B.E. / B.Tech for JE, and the relevant nursing / pharmacy / lab qualification for paramedical posts. Selection is one or two computer-based tests, followed (for some posts) by a skill, typing or aptitude test, then document verification and a medical exam.

value.title: At a glance
items: Application volumes are very large — often lakhs to over a crore per notification — so competition per seat is high.
Medical fitness standards differ by post; ALP and some operating posts need high vision standards.
Engineering officer posts in the railways come through UPSC (ESE / IRMS), not the RRBs.
Notifications now follow an annual calendar, but exam and result timelines can still stretch over a year or more.
